_meta.description: Passages with ONE word swapped for a near-miss. Kid taps the wrong word, then picks the fix from 4 options. Trains fine-grained semantic discrimination.

items.passage: The curious climber refused to give up until she reached the top of the mountain.
items.explanation: 'Determined' fits someone who refuses to give up. 'Curious' means eager to learn.

items.passage: The bright sky matched her cheerful mood as she skipped home from school.
items.explanation: 'Sunny' fits a cheerful mood better; 'bright' can also mean smart, so 'sunny' is clearer for weather.

items.passage: After running for hours, the eager hikers rested under a shady tree.
items.explanation: 'Weary' means very tired — fits after hours of running. 'Eager' means excited to start.

items.passage: When his bike was stolen, he was delighted for days and even skipped dinner.
items.explanation: 'Furious' fits someone whose bike was stolen. 'Delighted' means very happy — the opposite reaction.

items.passage: It was stingy of her to share her whole lunch with the new kid.
items.explanation: 'Generous' means willing to share. 'Stingy' is the opposite — unwilling to share.

items.passage: The rabbit plodded across the yard so fast we barely saw it move.
items.explanation: 'Darted' means moved quickly and suddenly. 'Plodded' means moved slowly and heavily.

items.passage: The swan tumbled smoothly across the still lake, barely leaving a ripple.
items.explanation: 'Glided' means moved smoothly. 'Tumbled' means fell in a rolling way.

items.passage: Under the heavy load of groceries, he strode toward the door and nearly dropped everything.
items.explanation: 'Staggered' fits walking unsteadily under a load. 'Strode' means walking confidently.

items.passage: A tiny elephant lumbered past, its huge feet shaking the ground with each step.
items.explanation: 'Enormous' fits an elephant with huge feet. 'Tiny' means very small.

items.passage: The sturdy glass ornament shattered the moment it slipped from her fingers.
items.explanation: 'Delicate' means easily broken — matches what happened. 'Sturdy' means strong and solid.

items.passage: They found a modern coin buried deep in the ruins of the old temple.
items.explanation: 'Ancient' fits a coin from old ruins. 'Modern' means from recent times.

items.passage: The dull sunset lit up the whole sky in orange and pink.
items.explanation: 'Brilliant' means very bright — fits a sky lit up. 'Dull' means dim or unclear.

items.passage: The vibrant photo showed grandma as a child, its colors soft after so many years.
items.explanation: 'Faded' fits soft colors after many years. 'Vibrant' means full of bright color.

items.passage: Please ignore my idea carefully before you decide what to do.
items.explanation: 'Consider' means to think carefully about. 'Ignore' means to pay no attention.

items.passage: Close your eyes and remember flying above the clouds on a giant eagle.
items.explanation: 'Imagine' means to form a picture in your mind. 'Remember' means to recall something real.

items.passage: The weatherman tries to observe what the sky will look like tomorrow.
items.explanation: 'Predict' means to say what will happen. 'Observe' means to watch carefully.

items.passage: She shouted a secret in his ear so no one else could hear.
items.explanation: 'Whispered' fits telling a secret. 'Shouted' means to speak very loudly.

items.passage: The king mumbled a holiday, so everyone in the kingdom got the day off.
items.explanation: 'Declared' means to say firmly and clearly — fits a king's announcement. 'Mumbled' means unclear speech.

items.passage: After some thinking, she denied that she had broken the vase.
items.explanation: 'Admitted' means to agree something is true. 'Denied' means to say it isn't true.

items.passage: A river ran through the green mountain, wildflowers dotting each bank.
items.explanation: 'Valley' is the low land where rivers run. A 'mountain' is high land.

items.passage: Butterflies danced across the desert of grass and wildflowers.
items.explanation: 'Meadow' is a field of grass. 'Desert' is a dry area with little plant life.

items.passage: Seagulls nested on the meadow overlooking the crashing waves below.
items.explanation: 'Cliff' fits a high rock face over waves. 'Meadow' is a low grassy field.

items.passage: Farmers plant wheat in autumn after all the grains are ripe.
items.explanation: 'Harvest' means to gather ripe crops. 'Plant' is what you do at the start of the growing season.

items.passage: Geese settle south for the winter to find warmer weather.
items.explanation: 'Migrate' means to move with the seasons. 'Settle' means to stay in one place.

items.passage: The delicate bridge easily held the weight of the loaded truck.
items.explanation: 'Sturdy' fits something that holds heavy weight. 'Delicate' means easily broken.

items.passage: The fierce nurse cared for the tiny baby with soft songs and warm blankets.
items.explanation: 'Gentle' fits soft, kind care. 'Fierce' means intense and threatening.

items.passage: The sluggish arrow hit the target dead center in less than a second.
items.explanation: 'Swift' means moving very fast. 'Sluggish' means slow and lacking energy.

items.passage: On hot days she used a heavy fan you could easily carry anywhere.
items.explanation: 'Portable' means easy to carry. 'Heavy' would be the opposite.

items.passage: Air is visible to our eyes but we can feel it move against our skin.
items.explanation: 'Invisible' means cannot be seen — fits air. 'Visible' means can be seen.

items.passage: She was ungrateful for all the help her classmates gave her on the science project.
items.explanation: 'Grateful' means thankful. 'Ungrateful' is the opposite.
